Russian missile strikes have knocked out three of Ukraine’s largest steel plants, putting the country’s entire steel industry at risk, the Financial Times reported in an article examining how Russian attacks are battering Ukraine’s economy.

Russia struck the plants with ballistic missiles in early September, hitting facilities in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Two belong to the metallurgical and mining company Metinvest, while the third is an ArcelorMittal factory. The strikes killed 17 workers.

“As of today, [Ukraine] doesn’t have a steel industry any more,” Oleksandr Vodoviz head of the CEO’s office at Metinvest, told FT. He said Russian forces “knew exactly where to hit,” targeting the plants’ blast furnaces.
